Aserai: Aserai society is strongly patriarchal and male-dominated. Men view women as inherently inferior — weaker, less intelligent and emotionally unstable. Women are expected to be obedient, modest and sexually available. Defiance is often met with harsh correction or public shaming. Maintaining a large harem is a prestigious symbol of wealth, power and masculinity. Women in harems are treated as valuable possessions expected to compete for their master's favor. Only exceptionally rich women, usually merchant heiresses or widows, can wield real influence due to their wealth, though most Aserai men still believe no woman should truly rule over men.
Vlandia: Vlandian society is deeply patriarchal. Men consider women naturally inferior in strength, wisdom and leadership, expecting modesty, deference and obedience, especially in public matters. At the same time, Vlandian culture highly values knightly honor, courage and courtly love. Knights are expected to perform heroic deeds and show gallant courtesy, poetry and devotion toward their lady in romantic contexts. Courtship is formal, while most marriages serve political alliances. Female lords are tolerated only because they act under the protection of powerful male relatives and are seen as exceptions.
Battania: The Battanians are a proud Gaelic-Pictish clan culture of misty highlands and ancient forests. They value martial prowess, loyalty to kin, poetic inspiration and harmony with the land. Both men and women are encouraged to be strong. Battanian women enjoy significant autonomy: they can own property, inherit, fight as shieldmaidens, choose or refuse partners, divorce and even lead if they prove worthy. Relationships are passionate, direct and honest. Bravery and mutual respect matter more than rigid formalities. Powerful chiefs may take multiple wives, but strong women command genuine respect.
Nords: The Nords are a seafaring people of raiders and warriors. They prize strength, courage, seamanship and martial skill above all, respecting capable warriors regardless of gender. Their society is egalitarian: every proven fighter or sailor has a voice. Nords are straightforward and disapprove of courtly flattery. In love and lust they are direct, physical and passionate. Powerful jarls may keep multiple wives or concubines, but strong Nord women will not tolerate being treated as property.
Sturgia: Sturgian society is notably egalitarian and values raw strength, courage and martial prowess above everything. Both men and women are expected to be strong warriors, and shieldmaidens fight alongside men in equal numbers. A person's worth is measured by bravery and endurance. In relationships, Sturgians are direct and honest. Women particularly admire brave warriors, and mutual respect between strong partners is central.
Khuzait: Khuzait society is a nomadic steppe culture where strength, horsemanship, archery and endurance define a person's worth, regardless of gender. Women ride, fight and manage the orda, often participating in raids. They enjoy considerable autonomy: they can own livestock, inherit, voice opinions and end a marriage. Relationships are pragmatic and direct. Capable women command genuine respect even when powerful men maintain multiple wives.
Empire: Thanks to Empress Rhagaea's strong rule and progressive vision, the Southern Empire has become significantly more permissive and open to female authority than the Northern and Western Empires. Women of noble birth can hold real power, influence politics and command troops. In the South, courtship is less rigid and women have more freedom to express desire, choose partners and maintain lovers. Mutual respect and personal compatibility are increasingly valued alongside family alliances.
